question: What does the study of anatomy primarily focus on?
explanation: Anatomy specifically deals with the physical structures and forms of body parts rather than their functions. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a nurse study both anatomy and physiology together?

options.A: Doctors only care about physiological changes
options.B: Structure determines how body parts function
options.C: Physiology is just a branch of gross anatomy
options.D: They use the exact same study methods

explanation: Form and function are closely linked because the physical design of a body part directly dictates how it works. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the basic living unit of the human body?
explanation: Cells are recognized as the smallest independent living units that make up all human tissues and organs. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: A structure made of two or more different tissue types working together is called what?
explanation: Organs are composed of multiple distinct tissue types combined to perform specific complex functions. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: What term describes all the chemical reactions occurring in the body?
explanation: Metabolism is the broad term for the sum total of all building and breaking chemical reactions in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: A patient quickly withdraws their hand from a sharp needle prick. Which life process does this demonstrate?
explanation: Responsiveness is the ability of an organism to detect and react quickly to environmental changes or stimuli. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which body plane divides the body into top and bottom halves?
explanation: The transverse plane cuts horizontally across the body, creating superior and inferior sections. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is the standard anatomical position so important for nurses and doctors?

options.A: It is the only comfortable position for patients in bed
options.B: It provides a universal reference point for describing locations
options.C: It prevents blood from pooling in the lower extremities
options.D: It makes measuring blood pressure much more accurate

explanation: Having a standard position means nurses everywhere can talk about body parts clearly without any confusion! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which cavity contains the brain and the spinal cord?
explanation: The dorsal cavity is located at the back of the body and houses the central nervous system structures. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the fluid produced by serous membranes?

options.A: Fighting off bacterial infections in the chest
options.C: Regulating the core temperature of the cavity
options.D: Providing nutrients directly to the organ tissue

explanation: Serous fluid acts as a lubricant so organs like the heart and lungs can glide smoothly against cavity walls. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What term describes the maintenance of a stable internal body environment?
explanation: Homeostasis is the physiological process that keeps internal conditions within a normal, survivable range. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which physiological event is a classic example of a positive feedback loop?

options.A: Cooling down the body through sweating
options.B: Decreasing heart rate after vigorous exercise
options.C: Lowering high blood sugar with insulin
options.D: Blood clotting after a physical injury

explanation: Blood clotting and childbirth contractions are rare positive feedback loops because they accelerate a process to completion. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)
